text: include implantation of biode- gradable polymers impregnated with carmustine (which has been shown to improve survival in patients with ma- lignant glioma),7 and the transient disruption of the blood- brain barrier to allow cytotoxics to cross. Other treatments investigated include single or multitargeted kinase inhibi- tors, ligand-toxin conjugates, antisense oligonucleotides, and gene therapy. Whole-brain radiation therapy is the common choice for most patients with brain metastases. Surgery may be suit- able for those with a single brain metastasis, especially if prognosis is favourable and systemic disease controlled.16 The value of chemotherapy in cerebral metastatic disease remains to be defined:8,17 the primary tumour may be in- trinsically resistant to chemotherapy, or metastasis may develop despite treatment of the primary tumour, which will encourage the selection of resistant species. Further- more, although the blood-brain barrier may not be com- pletely intact in these patients, allowing some passage of antineoplastics into the brain, drug delivery of the less lip- id-soluble drugs to cerebral metastases may not be suffi- cient, or sufficiently consistent, to produce a response. Nonetheless cerebral metastases of some chemosensitive primary tumours may respond to therapy.
